sections.body_md: Active stratovolcano at 2,386 m with the world's largest acidic crater lake and the pre-dawn blue fire phenomenon. Night hike from the Paltuding trailhead (~3 km). BBKSDA East Java is the regulatory authority. Health-certificate coordination is mandatory for every guest under BBKSDA SE.1658/KSA.9/2024.

blocks.body_md:
## The Blue Fire

Inside Ijen's crater, sulfuric gases emerge from vents under pressure and ignite on contact with the air, burning an electric blue. The flames are visible only in darkness — which is why JVTO groups depart for the rim around midnight and descend toward the crater floor before first light.

It is one of only a handful of places on earth where the effect occurs at this scale. The reward at sunrise — a turquoise acidic lake filling the crater — is extraordinary in its own right.

> **Weather & gas conditions apply.** The blue fire is a natural phenomenon, subject to weather and volcanic gas activity. It is not guaranteed on any given night. We plan around the optimal viewing window — we do not promise an outcome we cannot control.

## The Hike — Paltuding to the crater rim

1. **Departure timing** — 00:00 for the blue-fire window; 03:00 for sunrise only. Your guide confirms the plan based on conditions.
2. **The ascent** — ~3 km one-way from the Paltuding trailhead, roughly 90 minutes of steady switchbacks to the crater rim.
3. **Optional crater descent** — a steeper ~700 m path drops to the crater floor for the closest blue-fire view. Optional, and only when conditions and your guide allow.

| | |
|---|---|
| Distance (one-way) | ~3 km |
| Ascent time | ~90 min |
| Trailhead | Paltuding |
| Crater descent | ~700 m (optional) |

Equipment provided by JVTO: **gas masks** · **headlamps**.

## Health Certificate Coordination

**Mandatory · BBKSDA SE.1658/KSA.9/2024.** A recent health certificate is mandatory for every guest before Kawah Ijen crater entry. JVTO coordinates the clinic workflow — there is nothing for you to arrange separately. The BSrE-signed surat sehat is issued through Dr. Ahmad Irwandanu (SIP, Kemenkes RI) and is checked at the crater access gate.

> **Coordinated for every guest.** This is a regulatory step under BBKSDA, not a JVTO-imposed formality. Oxygen saturation, blood pressure, heart rate and respiratory history are recorded before crater access, at the guest's hotel. No valid health certificate, no crater entry — that requirement is BBKSDA's.

→ [How Ijen health screening works](/travel-guide/ijen-health-screening)

## Sulfur Miners — a shared working path

The trail you climb is a working route. Local miners carry 70–90 kg loads of sulfur blocks from the crater floor by hand — daily, at the same pre-dawn hours visitors are ascending. JVTO guides brief every group before departure: move aside for load-carriers, and never photograph a miner without first asking.

The mining operation is part of the reality of Ijen — a human one, not a photographic attraction. The briefing is standard on every Ijen route, not optional.
